title: Hazel and the Ledger
premise: In the river city of Vellmark, 1847, Freya Dunmore cuts typefaces by day in her father's print shop while revolution simmers in the streets. When the winter bridge closes and the authorities seal the city, her father's hidden ledger of debts and names becomes the most dangerous document in Vellmark. Freya must decide whether to burn it, publish it, or trade it — knowing the last berth on the smugglers' boat out can save only one of her family. In the end, she publishes the ledger at the cost of her father's life, and escapes alone, carrying the truth as her inheritance.
about_author: August Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing printers' records from nineteenth-century European uprisings. Ashgrove writes historical fiction about ordinary hands that move history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. We meet the Dunmore print shop: her father Aldous cutting typefaces, her brother Tam running errands for both printers and smugglers. Freya takes quiet pride in her invisible craft. Emotional beat: contentment built on willful blindness — she notices the city's unrest but chooses her letters over the news.

chapters.title: Ink on the Wind
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Rumors of revolution harden; soldiers patrol the printing quarter. A stranger commissions a pamphlet whose type Freya recognizes as her father's secret work. Emotional beat: first crack in the family's safety — Freya realizes Aldous has been printing sedition for money.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The winter bridge shuts and garrisons seal the city gates. Tam, who knows the smugglers' routes, reports the last berth on the spring boat — one seat. Emotional beat: dread and dark excitement; Tam sees escape as his due, not a choice to be shared.

chapters.title: What Father Hid
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Searching for pamphlet plates, Freya finds the ledger: names of officials, debts, bribes — proof that could topple the magistrate or hang her father. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into fear; the man she trusted has been gambling with all their lives.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Offer
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. The magistrate summons Aldous, revealing he knows about the ledger and offers the family's safety — and a second berth — if Aldous surrenders it and names his co-conspirators. Emotional beat: Aldous's rationalization; he believes sacrifice of others is the price of protecting his children.

chapters.title: Brother's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam discovers the ledger and the magistrate's offer, and begins quietly bargaining for the berth for himself, even offering information to the magistrate's men. Emotional beat: corrosive ambition — loyalty bending into betrayal one small deal at a time.

chapters.title: Night of the Presses
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Rioters storm the printing quarter; the shop is ransacked. Freya saves the ledger and hides it inside a case of type she casts herself. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve — for the first time, Freya chooses to act rather than endure.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Alternating Freya/Tam POV. Tam sells a partial list of names to buy his berth; a printer friend is arrested because of it. Freya confronts him on the frozen quay. Emotional beat: grief and fury — the family's love revealed as a ledger of its own, every entry a debt.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, climax. Freya prints the ledger as a broadsheet and scatters it through the city; the magistrate's power collapses into chaos, but Aldous is taken in the reprisal. At the quay, Tam holds the berth papers. Emotional beat: the terrible clarity of sacrifice — truth purchased at the highest price.

chapters.title: Spring Water
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, resolution. In the confusion of the uprising, Freya and Tam both reach the boat; there is room for one. Tam, changed, pushes the berth to her and vanishes into the crowd. Freya sails out past the broken bridge, a single type-slug in her pocket. Emotional beat: sorrowful survival — she lives, carrying the truth and the cost.
